churches.pastor_credentials: Credentials not published on website; lead pastor through denominational transition

churches.assessment: Aldersgate Church in Lubbock was founded in 1985 when a preacher began knocking on doors inviting people to a new church experience — the first service was held August 4, 1985 in the gymnasium of All Saints Episcopal School. The congregation voted 97% to disaffiliate from the UMC and has joined the Global Methodist Church. Lead Pastor Ryan Smallwood (married to Amy, two adult sons Blake and Jeb) leads with a conversational teaching style. Notable: Emily Fisher serves as Next Gen Pastor, meaning women do serve in pastoral roles at this particular local church — a YELLOW flag on the gender rubric for readers committed to strictly male-only pastoral offices. The lopsided disaffiliation vote signals strong institutional orthodox commitment, however. Named for John Wesley's famous May 1738 Aldersgate Street conversion experience.

churches.pastor: Dr. Joe Samuel Ratliff (Senior Pastor since 1980)
churches.denomination_detail: Southern Baptist Convention via the National African-American Fellowship of the SBC (NAAF) — Dr. Ratliff is the founding president of NAAF; also affiliated with Union Baptist Association (the largest urban SBC association in the US, where Ratliff was the first African-American to lead).

score_notes.gender: RED — Brentwood Baptist Houston has multiple ordained female ministers on pastoral staff: Rev. Mary A. Frazier (Minister of Youth & College since 2006), Rev. Barbara A. Thomas (Children & Events Coordinator, explicitly licensed and ordained). This is a direct BF&M 2000 Article VI nonconformity. Common in some Black SBC-affiliated congregations but technically grounds for SBC Credentials Committee review per the Saddleback / Fern Creek / Saddleback precedent.
score_notes.denominational: SBC affiliation legitimate via NAAF and Union Baptist Association, but female ordination practice creates BF&M2000 tension. Yellow rather than red on denominational because the church remains in formal cooperation despite the gender-policy gap.
score_notes.cultural: Site copy includes 'Social Justice Advocate' role (Dr. C. Clay Pickens) — verify whether DEI/CRT-adjacent or biblical justice framing.

review_flag.reason: Female ordained pastoral staff (Rev. Frazier, Rev. Thomas) at SBC-affiliated megachurch — should be referred to SBC Credentials Committee per Saddleback precedent.

churches.assessment: Brentwood Baptist Church Houston, led by Dr. Joe Samuel Ratliff since February 1980, grew from 500 members to 12,000 by 2000 (now ~7,000+ at two services). Dr. Ratliff is the founding president of the National African-American Fellowship of the SBC and was the first African-American to lead the Union Baptist Association (largest urban SBC body, 500+ churches). Theologically conservative on most matters (Christology, Scripture, soteriology) but ordains women to pastoral office (Rev. Mary A. Frazier as Minister of Youth & College; Rev. Barbara A. Thomas licensed and ordained Children & Events Coordinator) — direct BF&M 2000 Article VI violation. RED on gender; YELLOW overall with Credentials Committee referral flag.

churches.assessment: FLAG: BLACK (LGBTQ-AFFIRMING). Broadway Baptist Church was expelled from the Southern Baptist Convention in 2009 and left the Baptist General Convention of Texas in 2010 over its LGBTQ stance. Senior Pastor Ryon Price has explicitly stated his vision for the church to be 'more fully inclusive and affirming of all persons, including women, persons of color, and those in the LGBTQ community.' The church has added an LGBTQ+ section to its library, partners with CBF (Cooperative Baptist Fellowship), and pursues a progressive social justice agenda including feminist theology and anti-patriarchy. This church stands in direct opposition to biblical sexuality, complementarian gender roles, and historic Baptist theology. NOT RECOMMENDED — BLACK rating across gender and cultural categories.

churches.assessment: Christ Church Waco is an ACNA parish in the Diocese of Fort Worth, led by Priest-in-Charge Fr. Jeff Logan, who arrived in October 2025 after 22 years as a Navy chaplain. His academic credentials are unusually strong: B.A. from DePauw, M.Div. from the Episcopal Theological Seminary of the Southwest, and D.Min. from Fuller Theological Seminary. The parish maintains a full liturgical rhythm: Sunday 8:00 AM and 10:45 AM Holy Eucharist with 9:30 AM Catechesis, plus a Wednesday Noon Eucharist. Supported by Fr. Andrew Hollinger (Diocesan Curate, M.Div. Nashotah House 2024) and Rev. Thomas Hunter (Deacon, ordained 2024). Self-describes as 'a church of the great commandment, the great commission, and the Great Tradition.' ACNA 39 Articles framework aligns with MOOP's rubric. Strong green-rated Anglican option for Central Texas.

Headlined the 'Biblical Patriarchy & Christian Nationalism' live panel with Doug Wilson, Eric Conn, and Dale Partridge. Affiliated with Church & Family Life network (Scott Brown). score_notes.leadership: Governed by a plurality of male elders (Joel Webbon and Connor Hensley confirmed). Elder-led with clear accountability.
score_notes.soteriology: Affirms the doctrines of grace (Reformed soteriology) — salvation by grace alone through faith alone. 1689 LBCF is explicit. Green.
score_notes.cultural: Explicitly counter-cultural against 'WOKE NONSENSE' (their words on website). Joel Webbon is a prominent voice in Reformed circles on Christian nationalism and cultural engagement. Conservative.

score_notes.mission: Great Commission focus affirmed through Reformed Baptist confessional framework and online ministry reach.

churches.assessment: Covenant Bible Church is a Reformed Baptist congregation in North Georgetown (Austin metro area) planted and led by pastor-theologian Joel Webbon. The church affirms the 1689 Second London Baptist Confession — one of the most rigorous and historically grounded confessions in Protestant Christianity — placing it firmly within the Reformed, biblical-patriarchy, and expository preaching tradition. Webbon is a nationally known voice through Right Response Ministries, openly advocating biblical patriarchy (he explicitly rejects the 'complementarian' label) and Christian Nationalism. He has headlined panels on biblical patriarchy alongside Doug Wilson, Eric Conn, and Dale Partridge, and the church is networked with Church & Family Life (Scott Brown). He has generated controversy for some of his political/cultural commentary — men should evaluate this directly rather than through secondhand coverage. The church's theological foundation is solid: Trinitarian, faith-alone soteriology, male eldership, expository preaching, and Great Commission focus. The one caution is independence — no formal denominational structure means accountability rests on the internal elder structure. For men in the Georgetown/Austin area seeking a doctrinally serious, unapologetically patriarchal church, this is worth a visit. Personal note: Connected to Joel Webb (Webbon) referenced in USMC Ministries network.

churches.services: Sunday Bible Study 9:30 AM, Sunday Worship 11:00 AM (broadcast live on KSAT-12)
churches.overall_label: Mixed — SBC men's ministry + Cooperative Program, but women hold Minister titles (validated 2026-04)

score_notes.christology: Affirms Jesus as 'the Son of God and co-equal with the Father,' both human and divine, who 'arose from the dead after three days' and will return 'personally and visibly to earth.' Orthodox Christology.
score_notes.scripture: Strong position: 'The Bible in its entirety is God's Word to us' and 'the sufficient authority and supreme and final source of truth for Christian beliefs.' Functionally affirms inerrancy and sufficiency.
score_notes.gender: Senior Pastor Chris Johnson (male). However, the church has women in ministerial titles: Megan Langan serves as 'Minister for Single Adults; Pastoral Care & Women's Ministry' and Tera Kouba as 'Minister of International/Asian Ministries.' Women hold 'Minister' titles — this goes beyond support roles. Yellow: not egalitarian in senior pastoral role but allows women ministerial titles.
score_notes.leadership: Senior pastor model with Chris Johnson. Staff of approximately 44 across ministerial, administrative, business, and facilities departments. 12 ministerial staff. References a 'lead team.' No visible elder board structure on website.
score_notes.soteriology: Clear grace-alone position: 'Salvation is God's free gift out of His grace to us' and comes 'only by personally trusting in Jesus Christ as God's offer of forgiveness.' Sound soteriology.
score_notes.cultural: No explicit DEI/CRT language detected. Church emphasizes Bible study integration across all ministries (same passage studied in Sunday School, worship, and small groups called 'Circles of Six'). Historic downtown church. Needs in-person evaluation.
score_notes.preaching: Unique approach: the same Scripture passage is studied across Sunday classes, worship services, and small groups ('Circles of Six'). This suggests a Scripture-centered, potentially expository approach. Television broadcast on KSAT-12 suggests substantive content.
score_notes.mission: Mission statement: 'to follow our Lord Jesus Christ, and to lead all others to a joyful life with him.' Extensive ministry portfolio: men's, women's, kids, youth, Spanish, Asian/international, recreation. Great Commission-oriented.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Dedicated men's ministry with 'Fearlessly Following Jesus' programming. Green for intentional male discipleship.
score_notes.denominational: References to Cooperative Program giving and traditional SBC missionary offerings (Lottie Moon, Annie Armstrong) confirm active SBC cooperation.
score_notes.validation_2026_04: Homepage fetched 2026-04-23 — no Wayback snapshot. Mission 'follow our Lord Jesus Christ, and to lead all others to a joyful life with him' confirmed. Address 515 McCullough Ave confirmed. Who-we-are/staff/ministries nav exists but not parsed on homepage. SBC affiliation, Chris Johnson lead pastor, and women in ministerial titles (Megan Langan, Tera Kouba) all from prior enrichment — homepage did not re-expose them. No Comer/Kendi/DiAngelo, no overt affirming/egalitarian language. Per refined SBC threshold (BFM2000 + men's ministry), prior enrichment confirms SBC Cooperative Program giving and 'Fearlessly Following Jesus' men's ministry — this would qualify for green EXCEPT that women holding 'Minister' titles (Megan Langan as 'Minister for Single Adults; Pastoral Care & Women's Ministry'; Tera Kouba as 'Minister of International/Asian Ministries') is a substantive yellow — not a red flag (no female senior pastor, no affirming language) but exceeds standard SBC complementarian practice. Yellow held.

churches.assessment: First Baptist San Antonio is a historic downtown SBC church (est. ~1861) led by Senior Pastor Chris Johnson. Doctrinally strong: affirms Jesus as co-equal with the Father, Scripture as God's Word and 'supreme and final source of truth,' and salvation as God's free gift through personal faith in Christ. Notable strength: dedicated men's ministry ('Fearlessly Following Jesus') and a unique Bible study integration model where the same passage is studied across all ministries. The church broadcasts on KSAT-12 television, suggesting substantive preaching. One concern: women hold 'Minister' titles (Megan Langan, Tera Kouba), which goes beyond traditional complementarian support roles while stopping short of 'Pastor' titles. The senior pastoral role remains male. Extensive ministry portfolio including Spanish and Asian/international outreach. Worth deeper evaluation — one of the stronger SBC churches in the directory with solid doctrine and intentional discipleship.
churches.gender_detail: Male Senior Pastor (Chris Johnson). Women hold 'Minister' titles: Megan Langan (Minister for Single Adults, Pastoral Care & Women's Ministry), Tera Kouba (Minister of International/Asian Ministries). 2 of 12 ministerial staff are women. Women hold 'Minister' not 'Pastor' titles. Senior pastoral authority is male.

churches.assessment: President Lyndon B. Johnson considered the First Christian Church in Johnson City TX his "home church." LBJ was baptized in 1923 at age 14 during a Pedernales River revival hosted by this congregation, joining the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ) on the conviction that the Disciples' beliefs aligned with his views (he had been raised in Baptist churches). The congregation was organized in 1903; the original sanctuary stood at 6th & Avenue E and the present church is at 401 E Cypress. Currently a Christian Church (DoC) congregation, reflecting the denomination's 1968 Restructure into mainline polity and subsequent affirming positions. Listed here for civic/political historical significance.

churches.assessment: First Methodist Church of Waco is a historic 1859 congregation that was among the earliest to leave the UMC and join the Global Methodist Church in 2022. Rev. Dr. Mike Voigts became Senior Pastor in May 2025 after serving as a professor at Asbury Theological Seminary — bringing academic Wesleyan depth to the pulpit. The church operates three campuses: the Main Campus on Cobbs Drive, the Speegleville Campus, and a Baylor Campus specifically reaching university students with a Tuesday 7 PM service. One flag worth noting: Rev. Dr. Blossom Matthews serves as Senior Associate Pastor, meaning this particular GMC church does appoint women to pastoral roles (distinct from formal elder ordination, which varies by conference). This places the church closer to the YELLOW end of the gender-rubric for readers committed to male-only ordination. For those comfortable with women in teaching/associate roles but male senior leadership, it's a solid orthodox Wesleyan option in Central Texas.

churches.assessment: First United Methodist Church in Midland, Texas was founded in 1885 — the first congregation organized in Midland. On November 5, 1977, 31-year-old future President George W. Bush married 31-year-old Laura Welch at this church's Glass Memorial Chapel; the Glass Chapel was completed in 1976, just a year before the wedding. The Bush wedding gives this church its primary national notability. Current senior pastor is Dr. Tim Walker, with Rev. Kurt Borden as associate. Like Highland Park UMC Dallas, First Methodist Midland stayed within the post-2024 United Methodist Church after the conservative Global Methodist Church disaffiliation wave. Per MOOP rubric this is RED at the denominational level given the post-2024 UMC departure from biblical authority on sexual ethics. Included for situational awareness about the wedding site of a former president and first lady.

churches.assessment: Highland Park United Methodist Church is a large historic Dallas UMC congregation (founded 1916) at 3300 Mockingbird Lane. George W. Bush was an active member 1989-1995 and volunteered in a ministry serving low-income Hispanic families during those years; the church is currently constructing the President George W. and Laura Bush Family Confirmation Center on the Mockingbird Campus. Rev. Paul Rasmussen served as senior minister 2013-2026 and stepped down due to Parkinson's disease; Rev. Matt Tuggle became senior minister in 2026. Highland Park is institutionally part of the post-2024 United Methodist Church, which removed "incompatibility" language around homosexuality and opened LGBTQ+ ordination and same-sex marriage at the 2024 General Conference. Conservative UMC congregations departed during the 2022-2024 disaffiliation window to form the Global Methodist Church (GMC); Highland Park stayed UMC. Per MOOP rubric this is RED at the denominational level even if the local congregation is among the more traditional UMC megachurches. Included for situational awareness about a former president's home church.

churches.assessment: Kessler Park UMC is an explicitly and proudly LGBTQ+-affirming congregation in the Oak Cliff neighborhood of Dallas. The About page openly states the church is 'United Methodist in tradition, progressive in theology,' takes 'the Bible seriously, but not literally,' and is 'a proud member of the Reconciling Ministries Network.' The home page tagline ('A reconciling community of hope') and a prominent rainbow logo make the posture unambiguous. The church stayed in the post-2024 United Methodist Church through the disaffiliation window — the wing that formally removed restrictions on same-sex marriage and LGBTQ+ ordination at the 2024 General Conference. Pastoral team includes lead pastor Eric Folkerth (a self-described 'activist'), children's minister Kay Ash, and congregational care minister Ken Kelley. The directory user's tip of 'apostate, steer people away' is consistent with what the church openly publishes about itself: a progressive-mainline framework that has formally abandoned biblical authority on sexual ethics. Not recommended for men seeking a complementarian, inerrancy-affirming, Great-Commission-centered congregation.

score_notes.christology: Christ-centered language: 'Christ centers us.' Gospel-centered identity. Affirms Baptist Faith and Message (1963 version — not the stricter 2000 version). Orthodox Christology.
score_notes.scripture: Affirms Baptist Faith and Message 1963 — notably NOT the 2000 revision which strengthened inerrancy and complementarian language. Scripture described as 'authoritative guide' but not 'inerrant.' Yellow for weaker scriptural authority position.
score_notes.gender: RED — Major concern. Pastor Jeff Warren has publicly stated: 'Jesus did not genderize the Great Commission, nor does God dispense spiritual gifts to his children according to sex.' The church states 'Both men and women serve equally alongside each other.' Women serve on Board of Trustees (Laura Dronzek as Personnel Chair), chair standing committees, and hold leadership positions. The church withdrew from the SBC in October 2024 specifically over the SBC's push to restrict female pastors. This is an explicitly egalitarian trajectory — the church left the SBC rather than conform to complementarian standards.
score_notes.leadership: Board of Trustees governance model with Deacons, Church Officers, and standing committees. Senior Pastor Jeff Warren leads with Ken Holden (Deacon Chair) and Ken Stone (Board President). Women serve on Board and chair committees. No elder structure — uses trustee/deacon/committee model.
score_notes.soteriology: Baptist heritage suggests faith-alone soteriology. Gospel-centered language. No works-based indicators.
score_notes.cultural: Large megachurch (10,000 members). Emphasis on 'cultural engagement' as a core value. The decision to leave the SBC over women's ordination signals progressive cultural alignment on gender issues. Verify whether other progressive positions follow.
score_notes.preaching: Unable to verify from website alone. Large megachurch format. Founded 1939 with long Baptist tradition. Verify whether preaching is expository or topical/seeker-sensitive.
score_notes.mission: Strong mission emphasis: 'leading all generations to love Jesus.' Spanish-language ministry. Dallas Baptist Association and Texas Baptists partnership for missions and church planting. Multiple service times. Active outreach.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Men's ministry programming exists. Green for intentional male discipleship.
score_notes.denominational: Withdrew from SBC in October 2024 over women in ministry issue. Remains affiliated with Texas Baptists (BGCT) and Dallas Baptist Association. BGCT is historically moderate. BF&M 1963 (not 2000) as doctrinal standard. Yellow — reduced accountability after SBC departure.

churches.assessment: Park Cities Baptist Church is a large Dallas megachurch (10,000 members, est. 1939) led by Dr. Jeff Warren since 2010. The church withdrew from the SBC in October 2024 specifically over the convention's push to restrict female pastors — a significant red flag for complementarian evaluation. Pastor Warren has publicly advocated for women in ministry, stating Jesus 'did not genderize the Great Commission.' The church affirms the 1963 Baptist Faith & Message (notably NOT the stricter 2000 version) and states men and women 'serve equally alongside each other.' Women serve on the Board of Trustees and chair standing committees. While the church maintains orthodox Christology, gospel-centered language, and active mission engagement, the explicit egalitarian trajectory places it in the RED category for gender/biblical design. The church remains affiliated with Texas Baptists (BGCT) and Dallas Baptist Association but has reduced denominational accountability after leaving the SBC. Not recommended for men seeking a church with complementarian convictions, but doctrinally sound on core gospel issues.
churches.gender_detail: EGALITARIAN TRAJECTORY. Pastor Jeff Warren publicly advocates women in ministry. Church withdrew from SBC (Oct 2024) over women's ordination restrictions. Women serve on Board of Trustees, chair standing committees. Church states 'Both men and women serve equally alongside each other.' BF&M 1963 (no complementarian language) as doctrinal standard instead of BF&M 2000.

churches.assessment: Resurrection Global Methodist Church is a young church plant established in September 2022 — essentially co-founded with the GMC denomination itself. Pastor Jason Nix came on as Lead Pastor in May 2023 with 15+ years of ministry experience. The congregation currently gathers at the Arlington Music Hall while establishing itself. As a brand-new GMC plant rather than a transitioned former UMC congregation, this church's identity is defined entirely by orthodox Wesleyan doctrine from inception — no legacy progressivism to unwind. The caution is typical GMC ambiguity on gender/elder policy (verify Mid Texas Conference stance) and the reality that small young plants often have less-developed men's ministries. Still, a green-eligible option for readers seeking a post-UMC-split orthodox Wesleyan church in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro.

churches.name: Ridgecrest Baptist Church
churches.pastor: Nick Dorsey (Pastor, Staff Elder) — Arkansas native; came to faith in high school, called to ministry shortly after; previously served as associate and senior pastor in multiple states; married to Kellie (met in seminary) with 5 children. Joel Bench (Pastor of Discipleship, Staff Elder; SWBTS M.Div., Greenville native, 10 yrs student ministry, 20 yrs MercyMe tour manager) and Justin Milton (Pastor of Family & Community, Staff Elder; SWBTS, Greenville native, at Ridgecrest since 2007) round out the elder team.
churches.pastor_credentials: Nick Dorsey: seminary-trained (specific institution not disclosed on site), prior senior-pastor experience in multiple states. Joel Bench: BA Texas Tech, M.Div. Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary. Justin Milton: BA Texas A&M-Commerce, M.Div. Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary.
churches.denomination_detail: Member of the Southern Baptist Convention (SBC) AND the Southern Baptists of Texas Convention (SBTC) — the conservative-inerrantist Texas state convention (vs. BGCT). Iglesia Bautista Hispana Ridgecrest planted from the church in August 1981.
churches.services: Sundays: 9:15 AM Sunday School, 10:30 AM Worship. Wednesdays: 5:45 PM Nursery/Kids/Students, 6:00 PM Adults.
churches.overall_label: SBC + SBTC — BF&M 2000, elder-led, expository, Reformed-leaning soteriology

score_notes.christology: Doctrinal statement explicitly affirms Trinity ("One Triune God eternally existent in three persons"), virgin birth, two natures in one Person of Christ, substitutionary atonement, bodily resurrection, ascension, and return in glory — fully Nicene/Chalcedonian.
score_notes.scripture: Verbal plenary inspiration: "the Holy Scriptures are the very Word of God, verbally inspired in all parts and therefore wholly without mixture of error as originally revealed." Adopts BF&M 2000 verbatim. Inerrancy explicit.
score_notes.gender: Male-only elders/pastors confirmed via leadership page (all three Staff Elders are men; only role given to a woman is Minister to Children and Director of Nursery Ministry, consistent with complementarian SBC norm). BF&M 2000 adoption locks in complementarian pastoral office.
score_notes.leadership: Polity explicitly stated: 'We are ruled by Jesus, led by the Elders, and governed by the congregation.' Plurality of male elders (Dorsey, Bench, Milton) with congregational accountability — the textbook elder-led congregational pattern advocated by 9Marks. Pastor answerable to the elder team and to the congregation.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed-Baptist soteriology in the doctrinal essentials: total depravity ('man... has become separated from, and spiritually dead to God through Adam’s sin... possessing depraved human nature with no spark of divine life'), monergistic grace ('salvation is a free and permanent gift of God that cannot be secured or merited in part or in whole by any virtue or good work of man'), substitutionary atonement, perseverance ('salvation is inextricably bound to righteous living and good works and is the inevitable consequence (not the procuring cause) of the new life implanted by the Holy Spirit'). Faith alone explicit.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT or progressive-justice framing found anywhere on site. SBTC affiliation is the conservative Texas convention (split from BGCT in 1998 over inerrancy and trajectory). Stated mission language is gospel-centered ('herald... gracious proclamation of the Gospel').
score_notes.preaching: 'Our normal method of teaching is a verse-by-verse study of a book of the Bible.' Expository confirmed. Sermon archive shows 6,321 messages across 58+ series including book studies of John, Galatians, Colossians, Ephesians, Habakkuk, Esther, Philemon, 1 Timothy, Hebrews, Psalms, and Sermon on the Mount — systematic exposition over years.
score_notes.mission: Strong outward focus: 'Grow. Serve. Go.' core. Local missions arm 'For the City' (launched 2017) plus adopted missionaries (Adopted Missions Request form). Hispanic plant in 1981. Great Commission framed as primary purpose statement.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Dedicated 'RidgeMen Ministry' — explicit goal: 'equip men to build Christ-centered relationships through Bible study, service, leadership, and community.' Led by Joel Bench (Pastor of Discipleship). Independent men's page and contact path confirmed.
score_notes.denominational: Dual-aligned SBC + SBTC. SBTC is the conservative-inerrantist alternative to BGCT. Elder plurality plus congregational governance plus dual denominational accountability is among the tightest accountability structures available in SBC life.

churches.assessment: Ridgecrest Baptist Church in Greenville is exactly the kind of church the directory wants to surface: 60-year-old (founded 1965) conservative SBC congregation, dual-aligned with the Southern Baptists of Texas Convention (the conservative split from BGCT, not the BGCT itself), explicitly adopting Baptist Faith & Message 2000, led by a plurality of male Staff Elders (Nick Dorsey, Joel Bench, Justin Milton) under the polity statement 'ruled by Jesus, led by the Elders, governed by the congregation' — the 9Marks elder-led-congregational pattern. The 'reformed-ish' descriptor the submitter used is well-earned: the doctrinal essentials affirm total depravity, monergistic grace, substitutionary atonement, and perseverance, even though the church does not formally subscribe to the 1689 London Baptist Confession or claim a Founders Ministry affiliation on its public site. Preaching is explicitly verse-by-verse expository, with a sermon archive of 6,321 messages spanning systematic book studies (John, Galatians, Colossians, Ephesians, Habakkuk, Esther, Philemon, 1 Timothy, Hebrews, Psalms, Sermon on the Mount). The 'RidgeMen' men's ministry is dedicated and pastor-led. The local missions arm 'For the City' (launched 2017) and a Spanish-language plant from 1981 demonstrate Great Commission seriousness. Past pastoral roster (Pratt, McGinlay, Hamilton, Stubblefield, Douglass, Herbert, Beasley, now Dorsey) shows stable conservative trajectory. No drift signals, no female pastoral roles above women's ministry, no progressive-justice language. Submitter Ben Collins's characterization — 'fairly conventionally conservative SBC church, led by a reformed-ish pastor with outstanding shepherding and preaching skills... a great opportunity for a strong male community' — is independently corroborated by the church's own published material. Solid GREEN, no qualifiers.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only pastors and elders (BF&M 2000 affirms male pastoral office; three Staff Elders are men; no female pastoral staff)
churches.enrichment_notes: Live-fetched ridgecrest.com on 2026-05-15 via curl with full browser headers. Site returns HTTP 500 status (WordPress error in footer is visible on every page) but serves full HTML body; all pages confirmed readable. Senior pastor Nick Dorsey identified from /leadership/. Founded 1965 and SBC + SBTC dual alignment confirmed from /whoweare/. BF&M 2000 adoption confirmed from /whatwebelieve/ (statement is BF&M 2000 verbatim). Expository preaching confirmed from /what-to-expect/. RidgeMen ministry confirmed from /men/. Past pastors list: William Pratt (1965-67), James McGinlay (1968-1975), Dr. Bob Hamilton (1976-1990), Dr. David Stubblefield (1991-2001), Dr. Sam Douglass (2002-2005), Kevin Herbert (2006-2010), Dr. Matthew Beasley (2012-2022), now Nick Dorsey. Disambiguation: this is NOT the larger Ridgecrest Baptist in Springfield, MO (pastored by Dr. Jeremy Muniz), which uses ridgecrestbaptist.org — search engines often conflate the two. The Greenville TX church uses the bare ridgecrest.com domain.

submitted_by.note: A fairly conventionally conservative SBC church, led by a reformed-ish pastor with outstanding shepherding and preaching skills. The church also has a healthy generational mix of seasoned saints and families in every stage of life. Strong growth, an anchor church in our community, presenting a great opportunity for a strong male community.

Dot Thompson into pastoral ministry in 1982. Now affiliated with CBF and Alliance of Baptists.

churches.assessment: St. Martin's Episcopal Church in Houston is the largest Episcopal congregation in the United States by membership and attendance. The Bush family — George H.W. and Barbara Bush — joined St. Martin's after moving from Midland in 1959, raised their five children there (including future president George W. Bush), and returned in 1993 upon leaving the White House. President George H.W. Bush's 2018 funeral was held at St. Martin's. Rev. Russell Levenson Jr. served as rector 2007-2024, and Rev. Dane Boston (formerly Dean of Trinity Episcopal Cathedral, Columbia SC) was installed in 2025. Institutionally TEC has fully departed from biblical authority on sexual ethics since 2003, ordains women as bishops since 1989, and performs same-sex marriages. St. Martin's under Levenson positioned itself as the more traditional mediating wing of TEC, but remained in TEC rather than departing to ACNA. Per MOOP rubric this is RED at the denominational level; included for situational awareness about the Bush family church.

churches.assessment: Sugar Creek Baptist Church is a large multi-campus SBC church in the Houston metro area led by Dr. Mark Hartman since 2002. Doctrinally, the church affirms Trinitarian theology, the Bible as 'true and fully accurate,' and salvation as a free gift through faith in Christ — all solid positions. The church appears complementarian in practice (pastoral titles for men, support roles for women) though not explicitly stated. Three campuses with multiple service styles including traditional, contemporary, and Spanish-language. Major concern: no dedicated men's ministry despite being a large church with 100+ staff. The church emphasizes community through Connect Groups and has strong mission language. SBC affiliation provides denominational accountability. Needs in-person evaluation to verify preaching style and cultural alignment.
churches.gender_detail: Male lead pastor (Dr. Mark Hartman). Pastoral and Associate Pastor titles held by men. Women serve as Women's Ministry Associates, Children's Minister, Preschool Ministry Director, Children's Elementary Director, Director of Pastoral Care. score_notes.christology: Affirms Jesus as 'the eternal Son of God,' conceived of the Holy Spirit, born of the virgin Mary, 'fully God, fully man.' Substitutionary atonement, bodily resurrection, ascension, and return. Orthodox Christology.
score_notes.scripture: Strong inerrancy affirmation: Bible has 'truth, without any mixture of error, for its matter' and 'all Scripture is totally true and trustworthy.' Scripture is 'the supreme standard by which all human conduct, creeds, and religious opinions should be tried.' Green — clear inerrancy position.
score_notes.gender: GREEN — Complementarian. All-male elder board (7 elders). Lead Teaching Pastor Benjamin Bolin (male). All pastoral/minister titles held by men. Women serve as 'Minister to Preschool and Children' (Pam Reigle) and in director/coordinator roles. Beliefs statement affirms: 'A husband is to love his wife as Christ loved the church. He has the God-given responsibility to provide for, to protect, and to lead his family. A wife is to submit herself graciously to the servant leadership of her husband.' Clear complementarian theology.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led governance with 7 male elders who 'serve to shepherd and to give oversight' (1 Peter 5:2-3). Lead Teaching Pastor Benjamin Bolin. Senior Associate Pastor Donnie Voss. Multiple ministers for specific areas. Strong accountability structure.
score_notes.soteriology: Comprehensive salvation doctrine: regeneration, justification, sanctification, glorification. 'There is no salvation apart from personal faith in Jesus Christ as Lord.' Sound Reformed Baptist soteriology.
score_notes.cultural: No explicit DEI/CRT language detected. Spanish-language ministry (Travis en Espanol). Community outreach ministries. Historic church. Needs in-person verification but no red flags from website.
score_notes.preaching: Title 'Lead Teaching Pastor' suggests teaching emphasis. Multiple worship styles (choir-led, band-led, Spanish). Unable to verify expository vs. topical from website alone. The strong doctrinal statement suggests substantive preaching.
score_notes.mission: Mission: 'helping people far from God know Christ through global, domestic, and local impact.' Global Mission Coordinator on staff. Community ministries. College ministry. Spanish-language outreach. Great Commission-oriented.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry found despite having women's ministry programs (CELC & WOW). Small groups and Sunday School exist but no men-specific discipleship. Yellow — gap for a church this size.
score_notes.denominational: Confirmed SBC via SBC.net directory; historic SBC congregation adjacent to SWBTS.

churches.assessment: Travis Avenue Baptist Church is a historic SBC church in Fort Worth led by Lead Teaching Pastor Benjamin Bolin with a 7-member all-male elder board. This is one of the strongest doctrinal profiles in the directory: explicit inerrancy affirmation ('truth, without any mixture of error'), comprehensive salvation theology (regeneration, justification, sanctification, glorification), clear complementarian position in beliefs statement (husband as head, wife submitting graciously), and elder-led governance. The church offers three concurrent worship styles (choir-led, band-led, Spanish) and has strong Great Commission mission language. The main gap is the lack of a dedicated men's ministry despite having women's ministry programs — an oversight for a church with otherwise excellent theological infrastructure. SBC-affiliated with strong denominational accountability. Recommended for evaluation — visit to verify preaching quality and cultural alignment in person.
churches.gender_detail: COMPLEMENTARIAN. All-male elder board (7 elders). All pastoral/minister titles held by men. Beliefs statement explicitly affirms husband as head of household and wife's gracious submission. Women serve in children's ministry (Pam Reigle) and support roles. No female pastors or elders.
churches.denomination_detail: SBC — historic Fort Worth SBC flagship tied to Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary.

churches.assessment: The Woodlands Methodist Church is the single largest church in the Global Methodist Church — 14,000 members who voted 96% to depart the UMC and join the GMC in 2023. That kind of institutional courage (leaving a denomination with all the attendant property and legal costs) signals a congregation serious about orthodox Wesleyan teaching. Rev. Mark Sorensen took over as Senior Pastor from the long-tenured Rev. Dr. Ed Robb in 2021, holds an M.Div from Asbury Theological Seminary, and has served the church since 2013. The church operates two campuses in the Houston suburbs, runs a preschool and a private elementary school, and offers 10 live and online worship services weekly. As with all GMC churches, the local stance on women as elders should be verified (the Texas conference varies), but the overall profile is solidly orthodox, Trinitarian, traditional-marriage Wesleyan.
